text: Start talking. At the same time, I will not understand why, because their voices, their signals overlap, right? And the SNR that I get is too low. Why? Because the voice, the power of the useful signal of a student, is interfered by the voice of another student. So the SNR that I measure for the voice of a student is too low. We have the power of one voice as the numerator and the denominator. Okay, there is noise, it's low, okay, but there is the interference power, the power of the other voices that interfere. So the SNR is too low, the SNR is too low, and I cannot understand. Okay. So in Wi-Fi, we have exactly the same issue, same problem. If there are several Wi-Fi cars that want to send data to the same access point, if they transmit their signals at the same time, we say that they are going to collide because they overlap, and the access point cannot modulate any signal correctly. So all the information will be lost. That's why.
